S.FORM: Too magte nē 'n lä too jaajun avan hag nen̄, Makē Gäräs.
S.TRANSL: Once upon a time, a woman married a man from up there, from Mount Ghäräs.

S.FORM: Taem nē 'n sinän, mon m̄eerat tē mät. Mon m̄eerat ēn mät, gamtō nen̄ tē lä natōn la nē ok woo m̄ahgen.
S.TRANSL: While she was pregnant, her husband died. And because he had died, the woman was left alone to give birth.

S.FORM: Natōn nen̄, m̄eem̄eerat nirō. Tē ätä tuwoo wōrō.
S.TRANSL: She gave birth to two boys. And she began to bring them up.

S.FORM: Ätä tuwoo wōrō va—van, wōrō tē rēgrēg –
S.TRANSL: So she brought them up for years and years, and the two boys grew up.

S.FORM: Rēgrēg nen̄ we, on too qēn̄, tēlēē tē hag to, nē tē vis mēn mon wēēwēē miimiini nen̄ sa: “Na tē van to lē karen.
S.TRANSL: One day, as they were big boys, the three of them were together, and their mother said to her children: “I am going to the garden.

S.FORM: La gamuu ga haghag, gamuu wōn jēn̄jēn̄ moomuu jēn̄ la, moomuu jēn̄ wōn a van lē mok qätä vēē, gamuu mētē lälä lee!
S.TRANSL: As for you two, you stay here. Now beware: if you play your marble game, if one of your shell marbles rolls over to my bedhead, then you must not pick it up!

S.FORM: On mok qaatō vēē nen̄, too naha tē hag to van nen̄.”
S.TRANSL: For under my bedhead, there’s something very special.”

S.FORM: Wōrō tē jēn̄ gēn ek.
S.TRANSL: So they began to play marbles with their shells.

S.FORM: Jēn̄ jēn̄ jēn̄ va–van, jēn̄ mon too nen̄ tē van laln̄i (nan) pela mon monwōrō mama nen̄.
S.TRANSL: They played on and on and on – but suddenly one of their marbles rolled all the way to under their mother’s bedhead.

S.FORM: To gēn nen̄, m̄o nen̄ nē tē vis mun nē sa: “E, Tahik! Nēk ēt lä ma mok jēn̄ laln̄ē nan pilo mon monwōjō mama nen̄!”
S.TRANSL: At this point, the elder boy exclaimed: “Hey, little brother! Go and get my marble under Mum’s pillow over there! ”

S.FORM: Tahēn nen̄ sa “O, Tuak! Na a lä ēs avōh, monwōjō mama ok ēn suu tuwoo wōjō sa wōjō a lä avōh; sa wōjō wōn jēn̄jēn̄, la 'n jēn̄ wōn van laln̄ē vēē mon monwōjō mama, wōjō a lä ēs avōh. Too naha ok van nen̄.”
S.TRANSL: “What, brother?!” replied the younger one. “I won’t go. You know our Mum has forbidden us to pick it up! She said that if we played marbles, and if a marble rolled under her bed, we should not go and get it. Because there’s something under there.”

S.FORM: Nē sa “Oh, ta, ga wē woo! Nēk ēt lä ma, °nen̄° va luwluw woo! Luwluw va woo nen̄!” 🌿
S.TRANSL: “No, no, that’s fine!” retorted the other one. “Those were just words. Come on, go and get it!” 🌿

S.FORM: Nē 'n turag vata hag m̄ērē heg, nē 'n lan̄ ajew pilo (mon /) laln̄ē vēē mon mon mama m̄ērē heg, m̄alan ēn row woo we, tun̄ ti vil!
S.TRANSL: So up he went, and he began to lift up the pillow and mat on his mother’s bed like this. To his great surprise, he suddenly saw some water begin to flow!

S.FORM: Tun̄ ēn vil vata m̄ērē heg, mon mama tē hag to lē karen.
S.TRANSL: When the water began to flow, his mother was still in the garden.

S.FORM: Mon mama ēn ron̄ vata m̄ērē heg, nē 'n ginteg sēwēl ma, ginteg ma ginteg ma ginteg ma m̄ērē heg va–van, nē sa: “Awah! Wēē natnatuk ēn qiseg na!”
S.TRANSL: As soon as she realised what was happening, she ran back down, ran and ran and ran as fast as she could. “Good heavens!” she said, “My boys have done something wrong!”

S.FORM: Ginteg ma m̄ērē heg la, nē 'n tuu tuwoo ätägäh vala tun̄ m̄ērē heg la, nē a wokem ēsavōh we;
S.TRANSL: And as she was running, she tried to stand in the way of the water, like this, but could not stop it from flowing.

S.FORM: nē sa “Awah, wēē natnatuk! Gamuu 'n qiseg nok na! Nek gēn wēē viivirin̄ ga wēwē, tun̄ ēn van nok mē, la nawnawon woo!”
S.TRANSL: “Oh boys!” she thought “You’ve really done me wrong! But now this is too late. The water has flown away, there’s nothing more that can be done.”

S.FORM: Magte nen̄ ēn häläqäg vata m̄ērē heg, nē 'n van nē 'n hag suu vata hōw roka nen̄ a Liwsal, nek gēn too vat gēn ek vaan inen̄, hahan Rotun̄.
S.TRANSL: The woman jumped in the water, and sat down there in the middle of the flow, up in Liwsal. Exactly at the place of a rock down there, called Rotung (‘River Woman’).

S.FORM: Vat avan / Vat, magte ok ēn häläqäg maken.
S.TRANSL: This rock is no other than this old woman, who had jumped in the water.

S.FORM: Nan vat tun̄ ok tē sēv to maken nen̄, vat ok vaan nen̄ hahan Rotun̄.
S.TRANSL: That rock’s the one hit by the waterfall; that is the rock we call Rotung.

S.FORM: Suusuu nen̄ tē pah gēn van nen̄ le.
S.TRANSL: And this is how the story ends.
